chunks: Uthman ibn Isa from Ali ibn Salim * said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

A verse in the Book of Allah that is unrestrictedly applicable. I asked, 'Which is it?' He said: The saying of Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, in His Book: 'Is there any reward for goodness except goodness?' It applies to the disbeliever and the believer, to the righteous and the wicked. Whoever is done a good turn, it is incumbent upon him to reciprocate; and reciprocation does not mean doing the same as what was done for him; rather, he must do good to the extent that he sees that by his action, he has attained the merit of the initiator.
ai.seo_question: What is the deeper meaning of 'Is there any reward for goodness except goodness' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the verse 'Is there any reward for goodness except goodness?' (55:60) applies universally to both the righteous and the wicked, establishing a general ethical obligation of reciprocity. The Imam distinguishes between mere mirroring of actions and the higher spiritual merit of responding with sincere gratitude, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *ihsan* (excellence in conduct) as a means of spiritual elevation regardless of the recipient's faith status.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 2.ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn Sālim who said, “I heard AbāʿAbdillāh (a) say, ‘

There is a verse in the Qurʾān that is unrestrictedly applicable [to all].’ I asked, ‘Which [verse] is it?’ He said, ‘The verse wherein Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says: Is there any reward for goodness except goodness? (Q55:60) – it applies to the disbeliever and the believer, to the righteous and the wicked. Whoever is done a good turn, it is incumbent upon him to reciprocate; and reciprocation does not mean doing the same as what was done for him; rather, he must do good to the extent that he sees that by his action, he has attained the merit of the initiator [of goodness].’”
